summary.text: 3 of 3 hidden signals for Ford have fresh data: 1 tailwind, 1 headwind, 1 neutral. The biggest mover is “F-150 owner complaints” (-42.7% vs the 3 months before). These are clues, not forecasts.

ai.text: Recent alternative data suggests a mixed picture for Ford right now. On the positive side, F-150 owner complaints have dropped significantly, providing a mild tailwind. However, rising U.S. average regular gasoline prices could create a notable headwind for big trucks. Meanwhile, the U.S. vehicle sales pace remains neutral.

signals.name: F-150 owner complaints
signals.metric: Owner complaints filed with NHTSA about 2023–2026 F-150 SuperCrew (gas), per month
signals.what: Complaints F-150 owners file with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. Complaint surges are how many recalls and investigations start.
signals.why: The F-Series is Ford's profit machine, and Ford has led the industry in recalls. Rising complaints can foreshadow recall and warranty costs.
signals.now: Owner complaints filed with NHTSA about 2023–2026 F-150 SuperCrew (gas), per month: 17 complaints/month (last 3 months, average), down 43% vs the 3 months before. Data through Sep 2026. In plain English: complaints have eased versus the prior few months. We read that as a mild tailwind for Ford.

signals.name: U.S. vehicle sales pace
signals.metric: Total U.S. light vehicle sales, annualized (monthly, BEA)
signals.what: How many new cars and light trucks Americans are buying, as an annual pace.
signals.why: A rising tide for the whole industry. Ford's U.S. sales tend to move with the market.

source.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

signals.basis: vs the same period last year
signals.now: Total U.S. light vehicle sales, annualized (monthly, BEA): 16.7M/yr pace (last 3 months, average), down 1.2% vs the same period last year. Data through Sep 2026. That's within the ±2% range we treat as normal noise, so it reads as neutral for now.

signals.name: Gas prices vs. trucks
signals.what: The average price drivers pay for a gallon of regular gas across the U.S., surveyed weekly by the Energy Information Administration and published on FRED.
signals.why: Ford's lineup leans on big trucks and SUVs. Expensive gas has historically pushed shoppers toward smaller, thriftier vehicles.

source.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

signals.now: U.S. average regular gasoline price (weekly): $4.40/gal (last 4 weeks, average), up 7.7% vs the 4 weeks before. Data through Oct 5, 2026. In plain English: gas is getting pricier, a headwind for big trucks. We read that as a notable headwind for Ford.
